newsitem.title: MACAO: N.Korea moves early to open skies, official says.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea moves early to open skies, official says.

text.p: North Korea will open its skies to overflights by world airlines in October, two months earlier than previously expected, a travel official in the Portuguese colony of Macau said Monday.

"The North Korean government will open its airspace next month," Wilson Ng, Pyongyang's official travel and visa representative, told reporters at the launch of a twice-weekly stopover in the colony by North Korea's flag carrier Air Koryo.
Ng refused to disclose details, other than to say that Pyongyang would grant commercial airlines from other countries overflying rights for flights between the United States and China.

The International Air Transport Association announced last month that the reclusive North would open its airspace to world airlines, including carriers based in arch-enemy South Korea, in December after 16 months of negotiations.
IATA said the decision would save companies operating in the region more than $125 million a year in fuel costs alone.
Airline officials have said the move could cut flying time between major cities in northeast and southeast Asia and the Russian Far East by between one and two hours.
The two Koreas remain technically at war after a bloody 1950-53 conflict ended with only a truce. The two sides have never agreed on a peace pact.

South Korea and the United States have proposed four-nation peace talks with North Korea and China to replace the truce. However, North Korea has insisted on bilateral talks with Washington, saying Seoul was not a party to the armistice that ended the Korean War.
